page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes stand in the right margin beside the "Sic illi" paragraph and the "Ut de Latino" paragraph. Running head at top, page number 175 at top right. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: hortantibus filiis durat mentem, senatumque rursus ingreditur. Aliud Thrasæ amici nonnulli autores fuere, defensionis inanæ ludibrium spontanea morte præveniret: subtraheret aures convitiis & probris. quorum ille suasum secutus, tædia incertæ vitæ abrupit. Sed haud scio, annon animosius, & humanitati convenientius, alii subjecerint: segnes & pavidos supremis suis secretum circumdare. Aspiceret populus virum morti obvium, audiret senatus voces quasi ex aliquo numine supra humanas: posse ipso miraculo etiam Neronem permoveri. sin crudeliter persisteret, distingui certe apud posteros memoriam honesti exitus ab ignavia per silentium pereuntium. T.xvi.Ann.

Sic illi pro suæ sapientiæ modo. Christianæ Christianum dogma. doctrinæ mysteria suggererent: culpæ sibi conscio culpam fatendam, delicto crimine, pœnam a judice infligam sponte subeundam: criminis vero objecti puro, ne causa sibi necis feratur, defensionem ad extremum non deferendam.
main_text.head: Clausas affectui, apertas veritati, aures judex immotus habeat.
main_text.p: Obsidant animum ejus preces, dona, ambitus, gratia, odium.
Ille, velut pelagi rupes immota, resistit: Ut pelagi rupes, magno veniente fragore, Quæ se[?]se, multis circumlatrantibus undis, Mole tenet.

Rupes immota.Ut de Latino Virgilius. VII Æneid. Piso infensas patrum voces, odia vulgi expertus, nullo magis exterri-tus est, quàm quòd Tiberium fine miseratione, fine ira, obstinatum clausumque vidit, ne quo affectu perrum-peretur. Huc illuc pelli & inflecti potest, qui se prius à constantiæ sede dimovit. qui vero in rationis & æquitatis centro se continet, ad extrema non temere cir-cumducitur.

page.notes: The scan shows a faint "(" after "Claufas" and some stray marks near the bottom edge; these are not printed text. The word after "Quæ" is doubtful ("fe(e" in the scan), marked [?]. The printed "Rupes immota" note is split across two lines in the margin and is given as one note. The "dogma." word in the margin sits beside a different line from "Christianum"; both are combined into one note. Spelling "Pifo" in the scan is read as Piso; the long s is written as s throughout.
